review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting native-speaker review. B1 bridge, unit 11: a NEW course-authored dialogue story (owner decisions of 2026-10-06: (1) Gutenberg texts are not adapted, so this unit does not adapt Unamuno's Niebla ch04; it teaches the lemma pack planned for that adaptation with an original plot; (2) Niebla is not used as the bridge's core). One pack item was deliberately NOT used: "suicidarse" (a theme the unit does not need); the slot is logged as dropped. For the Honduran reviewer: (a) "el conde" is a nickname for a rich, generous neighbor, not a real count; his "coche" is an old horse-drawn carriage he collects, since Honduran speech would say "carro" for a car; (b) "adelante", "murmuró", "advirtió", "interrumpió" are literary tags chosen for the pack; (c) the abstract words (eternidad, porvenir, anarquismo, psicológica, fisiológico, género) sit in the uncle's talk and should read as the speech of a retired, bookish man; (d) informal address is voseo (vos) among the family; the uncle and the conde use usted with each other.

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: Mario era un hombre distraído, y esa mañana había perdido la carta del banco.
sentences.english: Mario was an absent-minded man, and that morning he had lost the letter from the bank.

sentences.text: La casa tenía un sitio para cada cosa, pero Mario nunca ponía nada en su sitio.
sentences.english: The house had a place for every thing, but Mario never put anything in its place.

sentences.text: Una pared separaba la cocina del patio, y la carta, según él, había desaparecido de manera misteriosa.
sentences.english: A wall separated the kitchen from the patio, and the letter, according to him, had disappeared mysteriously.

sentences.text: La buscó debajo de la mesa, dentro de un libro y en el bolsillo de una camisa vieja.
sentences.english: He looked for it under the table, inside a book and in the pocket of an old shirt.

sentences.text: —¿Otra vez perdiste algo? —murmuró su tío Ricardo, sentado en su silla.
sentences.english: "Did you lose something again?" his uncle Ricardo murmured, sitting in his chair.

sentences.text: El tío Ricardo era ciego desde hacía diez años, pero oía todo, y se daba cuenta de todo.
sentences.english: Uncle Ricardo had been blind for ten years, but he heard everything, and he noticed everything.

sentences.text: —No es nada, tío —dijo Mario—.
sentences.english: "It is nothing, Uncle," Mario said.

sentences.text: Busco la carta de la hipoteca.
sentences.english: "I am looking for the mortgage letter."

sentences.text: —¿Y no hay que pagar hoy? —preguntó el viejo con calma.
sentences.english: "And is it not to be paid today?" the old man asked calmly.

sentences.text: Mario se puso blanco y se sentó en el suelo.
sentences.english: Mario turned white and sat down on the floor.

sentences.text: —Sí, hoy.
sentences.english: "Yes, today.

sentences.text: Y no tenemos el dinero.
sentences.english: And we do not have the money.

sentences.text: Es una desgracia terrible.
sentences.english: It is a terrible misfortune."

sentences.text: —No es el fin del mundo —advirtió el tío—.
sentences.english: "It is not the end of the world," the uncle warned.

sentences.text: Es un problema.
sentences.english: "It is a problem.

sentences.text: Y los problemas se resuelven cuando uno se calma.
sentences.english: And problems are solved when one calms down."

sentences.text: —Usted siempre dice lo mismo, y yo siempre estoy exaltado.
sentences.english: "You always say the same thing, and I am always agitated."

sentences.text: —Por eso hay que calmar primero al exaltado.
sentences.english: "That is why the agitated one has to be calmed first.

sentences.text: Venite acá, tonto.
sentences.english: Come here, silly."

sentences.text: Mario se acercó, y el viejo le apretaba la mano con cariño mientras hablaba.
sentences.english: Mario came closer, and the old man squeezed his hand with affection as he spoke.

sentences.text: Sofía, la sobrina, apretaba la otra mano de Mario, y le acariciaba la cabeza como a un perro.
sentences.english: Sofía, the niece, squeezed Mario's other hand, and stroked his head as if he were a dog.

sentences.text: —No seas tonto, Mario —dijo la chica—.
sentences.english: "Do not be silly, Mario," said the girl.

sentences.text: Tenés que calmar ese corazón, y la carta va a aparecer.
sentences.english: "You have to calm that heart, and the letter will turn up."

sentences.text: —Yo no soy tonto —dijo él—: soy distraído.
sentences.english: "I am not silly," he said: "I am absent-minded.

sentences.text: Y ahora estoy peor.
sentences.english: And now I am worse."

sentences.text: Mario apretaba la silla con las dos manos, y no lograba calmarse.
sentences.english: Mario gripped the chair with both hands, and could not calm down.

sentences.text: —Un problema grave —dijo Ricardo— se vuelve más grave si lo ocultamos.
sentences.english: "A serious problem," said Ricardo, "becomes more serious if we hide it."

sentences.text: —No quiero ocultar nada —respondió Mario—, sólo quiero encontrar la carta.
sentences.english: "I do not want to hide anything," Mario replied, "I only want to find the letter."

sentences.text: En ese momento, alguien tocó la puerta tres veces.
sentences.english: At that moment, someone knocked on the door three times.

sentences.text: —¡Adelante! —gritó la chica, que se llamaba Sofía y tenía once años.
sentences.english: "Come in!" shouted the girl, who was called Sofía and was eleven years old.

sentences.text: Sofía había dejado al perro en el patio, y corrió a abrir con el pelo en la cara.
sentences.english: Sofía had left the dog in the patio, and ran to open the door with hair in her face.

sentences.text: Entró un hombre grande, con un sombrero de color café y una camisa larga.
sentences.english: A big man came in, with a coffee-colored hat and a long shirt.

sentences.text: Era don Fernando, al que toda la gente llamaba «el conde», porque tenía un coche de caballos de hacía cien años.
sentences.english: It was don Fernando, whom everybody called "the count," because he had a hundred-year-old horse carriage.

sentences.text: —Buenos días a todos —dijo don Fernando, y se quitó el sombrero—.
sentences.english: "Good morning to all," said don Fernando, and he took off his hat.

sentences.text: ¿Se puede?
sentences.english: "May I?"

sentences.text: —Adelante, adelante —dijo el tío—.
sentences.english: "Come in, come in," said the uncle.

sentences.text: Ya entró usted, don Fernando, pero no importa.
sentences.english: "You have already come in, don Fernando, but it does not matter."

sentences.text: —Es una burla, tío —dijo Mario, rojo.
sentences.english: "It is a mockery, Uncle," Mario said, red in the face.

sentences.text: —No es nada de eso —dijo don Fernando—.
sentences.english: "It is nothing of the sort," said don Fernando.

sentences.text: Es un modo admirable de saludar.
sentences.english: "It is an admirable way to greet.

sentences.text: Su tío es un hombre admirable, y a mí me da pena no tener uno igual.
sentences.english: Your uncle is an admirable man, and I feel sorry not to have one like him."

sentences.text: Se sentó en un sitio cerca de la ventana, y miró a todos con una mirada misteriosa.
sentences.english: He sat in a place near the window, and looked at everyone with a mysterious look.

sentences.text: Tenía una voz misteriosa, grave y lenta, y nadie dijo nada.
sentences.english: He had a mysterious voice, deep and slow, and nobody said anything.

sentences.text: —Me hace falta hablar con ustedes —dijo—.
sentences.english: "I need to talk with you," he said.

sentences.text: Es una cosa que importa, y para mí es terrible dejarla pasar.
sentences.english: "It is something that matters, and for me it is terrible to let it pass."

sentences.text: —Vine por una cosa de dinero —dijo—.
sentences.english: "I came about a matter of money," he said.

sentences.text: Es una cosa grave, pero también es una cosa buena.
sentences.english: "It is a serious thing, but it is also a good thing."

sentences.text: Mario miró a su tío, y el tío hizo como que miraba.
sentences.english: Mario looked at his uncle, and the uncle pretended to look.

sentences.text: —Vi la carta del banco en el correo —siguió don Fernando—.
sentences.english: "I saw the bank's letter in the mail," don Fernando went on.

sentences.text: Y quiero ayudarlos.
sentences.english: "And I want to help you."

sentences.text: —¿Por qué? —interrumpió Mario—.
sentences.english: "Why?" Mario interrupted.

sentences.text: ¿Qué gana usted con eso?
sentences.english: "What do you gain from it?"

sentences.text: —Nada.
sentences.english: "Nothing.

sentences.text: Es mi deseo.
sentences.english: It is my wish.

sentences.text: Un hombre tiene derecho a un deseo, ¿no?
sentences.english: A man has the right to a wish, does he not?"

sentences.text: Sofía se paró delante de él y lo miró con ojos grandes, y don Fernando se rió.
sentences.english: Sofía stood in front of him and looked at him with big eyes, and don Fernando laughed.

sentences.text: —Señor conde —dijo la sobrina del ciego—, ¿es verdad que su coche habla?
sentences.english: "Mr. Count," said the blind man's niece, "is it true that your carriage talks?"

sentences.text: —No habla, chiquilla —respondió él—.
sentences.english: "It does not talk, little one," he answered.

sentences.text: Es sólo viejo, como yo.
sentences.english: "It is only old, like me."

sentences.text: Sofía se rió, y le dio la mano a don Fernando, que acariciaba su barba.
sentences.english: Sofía laughed, and gave her hand to don Fernando, who was stroking his beard.

sentences.text: —Soy la sobrina de Ricardo —dijo la chica—, y también soy la que encuentra las cartas.
sentences.english: "I am Ricardo's niece," said the girl, "and I am also the one who finds the letters."

sentences.text: —Admirable —repitió Mario, que no entendía qué había de admirable en una chica con tantas cartas.
sentences.english: "Admirable," Mario repeated, who did not understand what was so admirable about a girl with so many letters.

sentences.text: Don Fernando puso su sombrero sobre la mesa.
sentences.english: Don Fernando put his hat on the table.

sentences.text: —Don Ricardo —dijo—, yo sé que usted fue anarquista de joven.
sentences.english: "Don Ricardo," he said, "I know you were an anarchist when you were young."

sentences.text: —Mi anarquismo fue un error de joven —contestó el viejo—.
sentences.english: "My anarchism was an error of youth," the old man answered.

sentences.text: Pero un error con ilusión, que es lo mejor del mundo.
sentences.english: "But an error with enthusiasm, which is the best thing in the world."

sentences.text: —Del anarquismo me quedó la idea de dudar de todo, incluso de los señores importantes.
sentences.english: "From anarchism I kept the idea of doubting everything, even important men."

sentences.text: —Un anarquismo sin pan no sirve —interrumpió Sofía, que había oído hablar de eso en la escuela.
sentences.english: "An anarchism without bread is no use," Sofía interrupted, who had heard about it at school.

sentences.text: —Tampoco sirve un pan sin ilusión —dijo el tío—.
sentences.english: "Neither is bread without enthusiasm any use," said the uncle.

sentences.text: Ese es otro género de hambre.
sentences.english: "That is another kind of hunger."

sentences.text: —¿Y hoy qué cree usted?
sentences.english: "And what do you believe today?"

sentences.text: —Hoy creo en el porvenir.
sentences.english: "Today I believe in the future.

sentences.text: No en el mío, que es poco, sino en el de ellos.
sentences.english: Not in mine, which is little, but in theirs."

sentences.text: Con la mano mostró a Mario y a Sofía.
sentences.english: With his hand he indicated Mario and Sofía.

sentences.text: —El porvenir de esta casa —advirtió— es lo que me preocupa.
sentences.english: "The future of this house," he warned, "is what worries me."

sentences.text: —Yo también pienso en la eternidad —dijo don Fernando—, pero con menos ilusión.
sentences.english: "I also think about eternity," said don Fernando, "but with less enthusiasm."

sentences.text: —La eternidad es una cosa para los que no tienen hipoteca —se rió el tío—.
sentences.english: "Eternity is a thing for those who have no mortgage," the uncle laughed.

sentences.text: Para nosotros, el único porvenir es el viernes.
sentences.english: "For us, the only future is Friday."

sentences.text: —La eternidad dura mucho —dijo Sofía—, y yo ya tengo hambre.
sentences.english: "Eternity lasts a long time," said Sofía, "and I am already hungry."

sentences.text: Don Fernando se rió también, y Sofía se rió con ellos sin entender por qué.
sentences.english: Don Fernando laughed too, and Sofía laughed with them without understanding why.

sentences.text: Mario seguía distraído, mirando la mesa.
sentences.english: Mario was still absent-minded, looking at the table.

sentences.text: —Se me antojaba que usted era un hombre importante —murmuró—.
sentences.english: "It seemed to me that you were an important man," he murmured.

sentences.text: Se me antojaba también que no tenía problemas.
sentences.english: "It also seemed to me that you had no problems."

sentences.text: —Todos tenemos un deseo, joven.
sentences.english: "We all have a wish, young man.

sentences.text: Es una cosa del género humano —dijo don Fernando—.
sentences.english: It is a thing of the human kind," said don Fernando.

sentences.text: Nunca somos lo que parecemos.
sentences.english: "We are never what we seem."

sentences.text: —No —interrumpió el tío—, déjelo hablar.
sentences.english: "No," the uncle interrupted, "let him speak.

sentences.text: En este género de problemas, el tiempo ayuda.
sentences.english: In this kind of problem, time helps."

sentences.text: —¿Y usted qué es? —preguntó el ciego.
sentences.english: "And what are you?" asked the blind man.

sentences.text: —Un hombre con mucho tiempo —dijo don Fernando—.
sentences.english: "A man with a lot of time," said don Fernando.

sentences.text: Mi mayor problema es el aburrimiento.
sentences.english: "My biggest problem is boredom.

sentences.text: Por eso compro cosas viejas.
sentences.english: That is why I buy old things."

sentences.text: —Si el aburrimiento fuera una enfermedad —dijo Ricardo—, sería psicológica.
sentences.english: "If boredom were an illness," Ricardo said, "it would be psychological."

sentences.text: —¿Qué es psicológica? —preguntó Sofía.
sentences.english: "What is psychological?" Sofía asked.

sentences.text: —Psicológica es lo que está en la cabeza —explicó el tío—, y fisiológica es lo que está en el cuerpo.
sentences.english: "Psychological is what is in the head," the uncle explained, "and physiological is what is in the body."

sentences.text: —O fisiológica —dijo don Fernando—.
sentences.english: "Or physiological," said don Fernando.

sentences.text: Mi médico dice que me falta sueño.
sentences.english: "My doctor says I lack sleep.

sentences.text: Si fuera fisiológica, dormiría más; pero yo digo que me faltan penas.
sentences.english: If it were physiological, I would sleep more; but I say I lack troubles."

sentences.text: —Aquí no faltan penas —dijo el viejo—.
sentences.english: "Here troubles are not lacking," the old man said.

sentences.text: Y para nosotros, la noche pasada fue una noche terrible, por falta de dinero y por falta de sueño.
sentences.english: "And for us, last night was a terrible night, for lack of money and for lack of sleep."

sentences.text: Mario se retiró a la cocina, y volvió con tres tazas de café.
sentences.english: Mario withdrew to the kitchen, and came back with three cups of coffee.

sentences.text: —Mirá, tío —dijo Mario, exaltado de nuevo—.
sentences.english: "Look, Uncle," said Mario, agitated again.

sentences.text: Dice que quiere ayudarnos, y no sé qué pensar.
sentences.english: "He says he wants to help us, and I do not know what to think.

sentences.text: Será otra burla.
sentences.english: It will be another mockery."

sentences.text: Don Fernando se retiró un poco de la mesa, y su cara cambió.
sentences.english: Don Fernando moved back a little from the table, and his face changed.

sentences.text: —Joven —dijo—, no hay burla en esto.
sentences.english: "Young man," he said, "there is no mockery in this.

sentences.text: Hoy mi aburrimiento terminó, y estoy dispuesto a todo.
sentences.english: Today my boredom ended, and I am ready for anything."

sentences.text: —Y mi tío, ¿qué gana? —preguntó Mario.
sentences.english: "And what does my uncle gain?" asked Mario.

sentences.text: —Mi propuesta es fácil.
sentences.english: "My proposal is easy.

sentences.text: Yo pagaré la hipoteca, y ustedes me dejan usar el patio para guardar mi coche.
sentences.english: I will pay the mortgage, and you let me use the patio to keep my carriage."

sentences.text: —¿Eso de cien años en el patio? —se rió Sofía—.
sentences.english: "That hundred-year-old thing in the patio?" laughed Sofía.

sentences.text: ¡Qué tontería!
sentences.english: "What nonsense!"

sentences.text: —Son tonterías de viejo, chiquilla —respondió él—, pero me hacen feliz.
sentences.english: "It is old men's nonsense, little one," he answered, "but it makes me happy."

sentences.text: —No hay que ocultar nada —advirtió el tío—.
sentences.english: "There is nothing to hide," the uncle warned.

sentences.text: ¿Qué más quiere usted?
sentences.english: "What else do you want?"

sentences.text: —Nada más.
sentences.english: "Nothing more.

sentences.text: Estoy dispuesto a firmar hoy mismo.
sentences.english: I am ready to sign this very day."

sentences.text: —Y yo estoy dispuesto a creerlo —dijo el viejo—, aunque la desgracia nos haya hecho tristes.
sentences.english: "And I am ready to believe it," said the old man, "even if misfortune has made us sad."

sentences.text: —Tío —murmuró Mario—, ¿se lo creemos?
sentences.english: "Uncle," Mario murmured, "do we believe him?"

sentences.text: El viejo guardó silencio un largo rato.
sentences.english: The old man kept silent for a long while.

sentences.text: —Hijo, hay un consuelo en la desgracia —dijo por fin—.
sentences.english: "My son, there is a comfort in misfortune," he said at last.

sentences.text: A veces llega un hombre que no esperábamos.
sentences.english: "Sometimes a man arrives whom we did not expect."

sentences.text: —No hay que creerle a cualquiera —dijo Mario.
sentences.english: "One should not believe just anyone," Mario said.

sentences.text: —Este consuelo —dijo el tío— vale más que mil palabras.
sentences.english: "This comfort," said the uncle, "is worth more than a thousand words.

sentences.text: Y es verdad, no es mentira.
sentences.english: And it is true, it is not a lie."

sentences.text: Sofía, la chiquilla, acariciaba la mano de don Fernando, y él la miró con cariño.
sentences.english: Sofía, the little one, was stroking don Fernando's hand, and he looked at her fondly.

sentences.text: A Mario se le antojaba que todo era un sueño, y que mañana la carta aparecería debajo de la cama.
sentences.english: It seemed to Mario that it was all a dream, and that tomorrow the letter would turn up under the bed.

sentences.text: Esa tarde firmaron el papel, y Mario sintió que algo se separaba en su pecho, como una piedra que se retira.
sentences.english: That afternoon they signed the paper, and Mario felt something come apart in his chest, like a stone being moved away.

sentences.text: —Vuelvo mañana, sin falta —dijo el conde al irse, sonriendo.
sentences.english: "I will be back tomorrow, without fail," said the count as he left, smiling.

sentences.text: Y el tío se quedó en su silla, diciendo bajito: «Qué extraño es el mundo».
sentences.english: And the uncle stayed in his chair, saying softly: "How strange the world is."
